summary: Herbert Karl Alfred Plaeschke was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He studied at the University of Halle under Heinz Mode and Karl Ammer, earning his Dr.phil. and PD, and worked at the University and State Library of Saxony-Anhalt (c. 1959–1993).

Herbert Leonard Offley Garrett worked in history, archaeology, and Indology after studying at St John's College. He taught at Queen's College (1904–1912) and served as Vice-Principal (1919) and Principal (1927–1936) at Government College University, Lahore, and Syndic at Punjab University.
Herbert Mills Birdwood studied at the University of Edinburgh (c. 1851–1854) and Peterhouse (c. 1854–1858). He served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1858 to 1897.

Herbert Niel Randle was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Hertford College and Oxford (D.Phil.). He was Professor of Philosophy at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Allahabad, and served as Assistant Librarian (1927–1949) and Librarian (c. 1933–1949) at the India Office.

Linguist Herbert Petersson studied at Lund University under Nils Olof Mathias Flensburg, completing his Ph.D., and also studied at Rostock, Münster, and Copenhagen. He spent his career at Lund as Docent (1911) and ordinary Professor of Sanskrit and Indo-European linguistics (1923–1927).

Linguist and Indologist Herbert Pierrepont Houghton studied at Amherst College, Johns Hopkins (Ph.D.), and Princeton. He served as President of Waynesburg University (1908–1915), worked at Carroll University (1918–1920), and was Professor of Classics at Carleton College (1923–1950).
Herbert Schneider was a philosopher who studied at the City University of New York and Columbia University. He held an academic post at Columbia University from around 1919 to 1957.
Indologist Herbert Tower Sorley earned an M.A. from the University of Aberdeen (c. 1910–1914) and a D.Litt. from the University of Sindh.

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, Herbert V. Guenther earned degrees at Munich and Vienna. He taught at Vienna, Lucknow, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, then headed the Far Eastern Studies department at the University of Saskatchewan (1964–1984).

Herbert W. Duda was a linguist and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held academic posts at the University of Leipzig (c. 1932–1936), the University of Breslau (c. 1936–1944), and the University of Vienna (c. 1944–1970).

Linguist and historian Herbert Weir Smyth studied at Swarthmore, Harvard, Leipzig, and Göttingen. He held posts at Williams College, Johns Hopkins, Bryn Mawr, and Harvard University, where he served as Eliot Professor of Greek Literature (1902–1925).

Herbert Wilhelmy studied at the University of Leipzig (c. 1930–1932) and worked in history and archaeology. He held posts at Kiel University (c. 1937–1942), the University of Stuttgart (c. 1954–1958), and the University of Tübingen (c. 1958–1978).

Indologist and linguist Herbert William Magoun studied at Grinnell and Johns Hopkins (Ph.D. under Maurice Bloomfield). He held teaching posts at Grinnell, Colorado, Oberlin, and Redfield College, and was President of Massachusetts College of Osteopathy (1921–1926).
Herbert Zachert was a Japanologist who studied under Karl Florenz (c. 1928–1932). He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (c. 1948–1960) and the University of Bonn (c. 1960–1976).

Linguist and Central Asian specialist Herman Almkvist studied at Uppsala, Paris, Leipzig (under Fleischer and Brockhaus), and Collège de France. At Uppsala University, he served as Docent, extraordinary Professor in comparative linguistics, and full Professor of Semitic Languages (1892).

Indologist Herman Eildert Buiskool studied under Barend Faddegon at the University of Amsterdam, earning his PhD around 1934. He subsequently served as a conservator at Leiden University from 1936 to 1938.
Herman Frederik Eelsingh was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University from around 1904 to 1908, completing his Ph.D. under the supervision of Willem Caland.

Indologist and linguist Herman Kellgren earned his M.A. at Helsinki and studied under Brockhaus, Bopp, Fleischer, and Burnouf, among others. In 1854, he was appointed Docent of Sanskrit at the University of Helsinki.
Herman Neubronner van der Tuuk worked in linguistics and Indology. He completed his studies at the University of Groningen (c. 1840–1843) and Leiden University (c. 1843–1845).
Herman Tieken is an Indologist whose academic career includes posts at Leiden University, attested in 2004 and 2013.
